tests.name: Player 2 firing out of turn is rejected with 403
tests.why: Turn order is a core game integrity rule — player 1 always goes first. If the server does not enforce this, any player could fire at any time, making the game unplayable. This test catches implementations that skip turn validation.

tests.name: Player 1 firing on a valid cell returns 200 with a result field
tests.why: This is the happy-path fire test — confirms the server accepts a legal shot from the active player and returns a result of hit or miss along with the next player's id. Without this working, no game can progress past the first move.

tests.name: Joining a full 2-player game returns 400
tests.why: Capacity enforcement must happen server-side — a client has no way to know the game is full without the server rejecting the request. This catches implementations that allow unlimited joins or only check capacity at game start.

tests.name: Move history returns 200 with empty moves array at game start
tests.why: A fresh game that just transitioned to playing should have zero recorded moves. An implementation that pre-populates moves, returns null instead of an empty array, or returns 404 before any shots are fired would fail this check.

tests.name: Player stats are initialized to zero before any games are played
tests.why: Stats endpoints must be usable from the moment a player is created — returning 404 or omitting fields like wins and accuracy before a game is played would break any frontend dashboard. This tests that all stat fields exist and default to zero.
